subject: series
synopsis: Ben Edlund's beloved superhero parody follows The Tick — a massively powerful, cheerfully dim crimefighter — and his moth-costumed sidekick Arthur as they protect The City from ludicrous supervillains, establishing the gold standard for superhero comedy.
author: Ben Edlund

subject: series
synopsis: Oversized collected edition of Kieron Gillen and Jamie McKelvie's acclaimed series about gods reincarnated as pop stars who live for two years before dying; a meditation on fame, art, and mortality.
author: Kieron Gillen

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's prequel series depicting young Fox Mulder and Dana Scully as teenagers in the late 1970s, establishing how they first encountered the paranormal and began their separate paths toward the FBI. Well-researched period detail grounds the familiar characters.
author: Jody Houser

subject: series
synopsis: IDW revival of the Beast Wars concept, presenting a new take on the animal-form Transformers in a fresh continuity.

subject: series
synopsis: John Ostrander and Del Close's 1987 DC horror anthology of strange, darkly comic short stories, drawn by David Lloyd and others.

subject: series
synopsis: Alan Moore and Dave Gibbons's twelve-issue deconstruction of the superhero: a murdered vigilante, a doomsday clock, and costumed heroes in a Cold War America.
author: CPY Document Author

subject: series
synopsis: Roger Stern and Bob Hall's 1984 four-issue mini in which Hawkeye founds the West Coast Avengers.

subject: series
synopsis: Comprehensive X-Men collection spanning decades. Multiple volumes covering different eras and storylines.
author: Roy Thomas, Len Wein

subject: series
synopsis: Robert Venditti's 2012 Valiant relaunch: Visigoth warrior Aric of Dacia steals alien armor from the Vine and returns to the modern world.

subject: series
synopsis: Haro Aso's survival thriller: aimless gamer Arisu and his friends are trapped in an empty Tokyo where deadly card-ranked games decide who lives.

subject: series
synopsis: Kieron Gillen's conclusion to the Krakoa era running parallel to Fall of the House of X, resolving the Moira MacTaggert storyline and the destiny of mutantkind through Gillen's trademark literary and mythological lens.
author: Kieron Gillen

subject: series
synopsis: An anthology series featuring Spider-Man in his black symbiote suit presented in stark black-and-white-and-red format, with rotating creative teams exploring dark chapters of Spidey's career.

subject: series
synopsis: A line of oversized hardcovers collecting IDW's acclaimed Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles ongoing series and its tie-ins in chronological reading order.

subject: series
synopsis: A Shuri-focused miniseries; Black Panther's sister with her own hero arc.

subject: series
synopsis: Dwayne McDuffie and Gregory Wright's 1991 Deathlok: pacifist scientist Michael Collins wakes up in a cyborg killing machine.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 1994 spin-off following Psi-Lord (a grown-up Franklin Richards from a possible future), Huntara, Devlor, and Nathaniel Richards as a team distinct from the Fantastic Four. A product of the team-proliferation era, the series struggled to find a distinct identity and was cancelled after 18 issues; a separate 2009 Fantastic Force mini-series featured a different lineup.
author: Tom Brevoort, Mike Kanterovich

subject: series
synopsis: Tony Isabella's 1986 Shadow War of Hawkman follow-up series, Katar and Shayera Hol against Thanagarian invaders.

subject: series
synopsis: Dynamite's continuation of the classic robot lion anime franchise, featuring the heroic Voltron Force defending the universe against the villainous Lotor and Zarkon. Brandon Thomas's 2011 run brought modern sensibilities to the vintage property.
author: Brandon Thomas

subject: series
synopsis: John Ostrander's original Suicide Squad (1987-1992): Amanda Waller sends imprisoned supervillains on deniable black-ops missions — Task Force X.

subject: series
synopsis: Chris Claremont's 2004 Excalibur: Xavier and Magneto rebuild Genosha after its destruction.
author: Chris Claremont

subject: series
synopsis: Justice League Europe renamed (1993-1994): Gerard Jones's overseas branch of the League, through Judgment Day.
author: Gerard Jones, Will Jacobs

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 2004 revival of the tryout anthology, opening with Fiona Avery's Araña, then rotating new characters.

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 1997 Challengers of the Unknown: a new set of plane-crash survivors investigate supernatural mysteries.

subject: series
synopsis: Abnett and Lanning's 2007 Nova: Richard Rider carries the Worldmind and the Nova Force through Annihilation: Conquest and War of Kings.
author: Fabian Nicieza, Evan Skolnik

subject: series
synopsis: John Byrne's 1999 Spider-Woman: Mattie Franklin takes up the mantle after The Gathering of Five.

subject: series
synopsis: Simon Spurrier's 2014 X-Force: Cable leads a black-ops team with Psylocke, Fantomex and Dr. Nemesis in morally grim missions.
author: Simon Spurrier

subject: series
synopsis: The annuals of the original X-Factor (1986-1994), crossover tie-ins and extra stories.
author: Mark Gruenwald, John Byrne

subject: series
synopsis: Boom Studios' series of original graphic novels expanding the Adventure Time universe beyond the main comic series, with various creative teams delivering kid-friendly self-contained stories in Finn and Jake's magical Land of Ooo.
author: Mariko Tamaki

subject: series
synopsis: Tom Taylor's run starring Laura Kinney (X-23) taking on the Wolverine mantle, celebrated for its action, emotional depth, and Laura's relationship with her clone 'sisters.' Features the acclaimed 'Immune' arc and strong character work.
author: Tom Taylor

subject: series
synopsis: The Golden Age anthology starring Captain America, the Human Torch, and the Sub-Mariner in early team-up adventures, historically significant as Marvel's first team-up comic and featuring early work that established the Marvel Universe's superhero tradition.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: A prequel manga to Attack on Titan by Ryo Suzukaze (story) and Satoshi Shiki (art), set a hundred years before Eren Yeager's birth and following the earliest attempts to understand and combat the Titans. Provides world-building depth for AoT fans curious about the Survey Corps' origins and the history of the Three Walls.
author: Hajime Isayama

subject: series
synopsis: John Allison's excellent Oni Press graphic novel series (spun off from his Scary Go Round webcomic) following the students of Tackleford Comprehensive as they solve supernatural mysteries they find far more interesting than any adult would consider advisable. Allison's sharp wit, eccentric characters, and genuine emotional heart make this one of the best YA comics series of its era.
author: John Allison

subject: series
synopsis: Eiichi Shimizu and Tomohiro Shimoguchi's Batman manga: a high-tech Batman in a power suit battles Gotham's rogues.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 1999 series following Bishop stranded in a post-apocalyptic future timeline, fighting to survive and find his way back to the present X-Men. A grim, action-heavy series that leaned into the dark future aspects of Bishop's character.
author: Joseph Harris

subject: series
synopsis: Osamu Tezuka's unlicensed medical genius operates outside the law, charging astronomical fees but performing impossible surgeries — each chapter a moral fable about life, death, medicine, and the human condition. A cornerstone of gekiga-influenced storytelling.
author: Osamu Tezuka

subject: series
synopsis: Shuzo Oshimi's psychological horror manga about a boy whose loving, devoted mother slowly reveals herself to be something terrifyingly possessive. A suffocating, brilliantly composed study of maternal trauma and its long shadow.
author: Shuzo Oshimi

subject: series
synopsis: Captain Canuck - Canadian superhero comic.

subject: series
synopsis: Len Wein's 2010 DC series narrating the history of the DC Universe through the eyes of an ordinary Gotham City citizen, tracing from the golden-age heroes through Crisis on Infinite Earths and beyond. A nostalgic tribute to DC's publishing history from one of the company's most distinguished veterans.
author: Len Wein

subject: series
synopsis: Reprint collections spanning the essential Daredevil runs including Miller's definitive work and subsequent acclaimed creative teams, making foundational street-level superhero material accessible in collected volumes.
author: Stan Lee

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel UK's 1983 weekly anthology, primarily reprinting Frank Miller's acclaimed Daredevil run for British readers alongside Captain Britain material. Historically significant as British readers' primary access to Miller's transformative Daredevil work.
author: Alan Moore

subject: series
synopsis: Disney's 2024 limited series spotlighting Negaduck, Darkwing Duck's evil mirror-dimension counterpart, in his own adventures separate from the hero's orbit. A fun villain spotlight for fans of the beloved Disney Afternoon animated series.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: All-ages anthology comics featuring various Disney Princess characters in original adventures, designed for young readers who love the animated films.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Matt Fraction and Mike Allred's charming companion series to Hickman's Fantastic Four, following a substitute Future Foundation run by She-Hulk, Ant-Man, Medusa, and Miss Thing babysitting Reed's genius students. Delightfully weird.
author: Matt Fraction

subject: series
synopsis: Matt Fraction's event featuring the Serpent, god of fear and Odin's secret brother, awakening to empower a new Worthy who wield Asgardian hammers. Notable for Thor's canonical death and the 'Worthy' concept, though considered uneven.
author: Matt Fraction

subject: series
synopsis: Geoff Johns and David Finch's 2013 New 52 event: the Crime Syndicate of Earth-3 conquers Earth, and Lex Luthor's villains must save it.

subject: series
synopsis: The third volume of Wildstorm's Gen 13 ongoing series.

subject: series
synopsis: Charlton's tie-in to the 1961 British monster film about a prehistoric sea creature captured and brought to London, whose mother then tears the city apart to retrieve it. Captures the kaiju spirit of the era and ran longer than the film's memory.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Walt Simonson's 2006 solo series spotlighting Kendra Saunders as Hawkgirl in St. Roch, Louisiana, dealing with the city's dark history and supernatural threats. Simonson's art is a highlight.
author: Walt Simonson

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's Epic Collection paperbacks reprinting Incredible Hulk material chronologically, including key Peter David and Bill Mantlo runs that defined the character's psychology alongside the early Lee-Kirby foundational issues.
author: Various (Peter David, Bill Mantlo)

subject: series
synopsis: Iron Man's post-Civil War role as SHIELD director, handling The Initiative's hero registration program and confronting World War Hulk; a solid if unspectacular period in the character's history tying into multiple concurrent events.
author: Charles Knauf

subject: series
synopsis: AC Comics' anthology series featuring jungle adventure heroines in the tradition of Sheena and similar Golden Age characters, primarily showcasing pin-up style artwork over narrative substance.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Chica Umino's quietly devastating series follows Rei Kiriyama, a teenage professional shogi player living alone in Tokyo, as he slowly opens himself to connection and healing through the people around him. One of manga's finest explorations of depression, found family, and recovery.
author: Chica Umino

subject: series
synopsis: Omnibus collection of Joshua Williamson and Mike Henderson's horror series set in Buckaroo, Oregon — birthplace of sixteen serial killers — where an NSA agent investigates what the town produces monsters.
author: Joshua Williamson

subject: series
synopsis: Stuart Moore's series following Namor establishing the Atlantean kingdom post-X-Men Schism, featuring a vampire invasion of the seas in a crossover with the broader Curse of the Mutants storyline.
author: Stuart Moore

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Evanier and Will Meugniot's sequel to their original DNAgents series (Eclipse Comics), following the team of artificially created superhuman agents in new adventures. Evanier's character-driven scripts and solid ensemble work distinguish it from generic superhero fare.
author: Mark Evanier

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's 2016 ROM relaunch by Christos Gage and Chris Ryall: the Spaceknight wages a hidden war against the Dire Wraiths on Earth.

subject: series
synopsis: Bongo's brilliant meta-superhero satire built around the Simpsons' fictional hero. Each issue parodies a specific era of comics history — golden age, silver age, Bronze Age — with obsessive period-accurate reproduction that works as both homage and comedy.

subject: series
synopsis: Jim Shooter's follow-up to the original Secret Wars, featuring the Beyonder walking the Earth as a human and confronting questions of desire, meaning, and mortality. More philosophical than its predecessor but considered self-indulgent.
author: Jim Shooter

subject: series
synopsis: Matt Fraction and Chip Zdarsky's sex comedy: Suzie and Jon discover they both stop time when they orgasm, and start robbing banks.
author: Matt Fraction

subject: series
synopsis: A 2024 Marvel series exploring the Spider-Man mythology across multiple dimensions, following the ongoing Spider-Verse premise of a society of Spider-people monitoring threats across the Web of Life and Destiny.

subject: series
synopsis: A 2024 Marvel anthology series featuring short stories about Darth Maul rendered in a striking black, white, and red visual style, exploring the deadly Sith assassin's hunts and battles across the galaxy.

subject: series
synopsis: Ethan Sacks and Luke Ross's 2024 Marvel mini: Jango Fett on a bounty hunt before Attack of the Clones.

subject: series
synopsis: Hirohiko Araki's sixth JoJo arc follows Jolyne Cujoh, JoJo's first female protagonist, imprisoned in a Florida maximum-security facility and entangled in a conspiracy connected to her father's old enemy Dio. Features some of the franchise's most inventive Stand abilities and a genuinely shocking finale.
author: Hirohiko Araki

subject: series
synopsis: Tom King and Bilquis Evely's stunning eight-issue series following a hungover, disillusioned Supergirl on a revenge quest across the cosmos with a refugee girl, subverting superhero optimism with emotional honesty.
author: Tom King

subject: series
synopsis: DC's quarterly Superman anthology running 1995–1999, publishing stories between the numbered monthly Superman titles and allowing creators more room than the compressed format of the weeklies. Featured work by various creative teams expanding the Superman mythology and dealing with storylines that didn't fit the main continuity books.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's comics continuation capturing the exact tone and animation-style of the original 1987 Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles cartoon, with Eastman and Laird's turtles in the bright, comedic Saturday morning format that defined them for millions of children.
author: Erik Burnham

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 2001–2002 series by the pseudonymous writer 'X' following a new Brotherhood of Mutants from a street-level, politically charged perspective — presenting mutant extremists as tragic, morally complex figures rather than simple villains. A deliberately different take on Marvel's X-Men universe that found a small but devoted audience.
author: X (pseudonym)

subject: series
synopsis: Simon Oliver and Tony Moore's darkly comic horror follows an exterminator who discovers a sinister pharmaceutical conspiracy lurking inside the company's pesticide supply — and the insect world beginning to bite back.
author: Simon Oliver

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's 2019 relaunch of the main Transformers series, beginning a new continuity with a fresh take on the Autobots and Decepticons arriving on Earth.
author: Brian Ruckley

subject: series
synopsis: Kieron Gillen's brutal continuation of his superhuman-soldier WWII series Uber, set in the decade following the war as post-war powers deploy their own ubermensch warriors in the emerging Cold War. Gillen's unflinching examination of the logic of power and atrocity extends into the geopolitics of reconstruction with the same rigor as the original.
author: Kieron Gillen

subject: series
synopsis: Robert Venditti and Riley Rossmo's 2023 mini: the Golden Age Sandman Wesley Dodds, gas mask and sleep gun, faces his first cases in 1930s New York.

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 1997 series by Dan Raspler and Dev Madan about a team of young superheroes whose interpersonal romances and shifting loyalties complicate their crimefighting. A charming, character-driven book that used the superhero framework to tell relationship stories, cut short after 17 issues but fondly remembered by readers who found it.
author: Dan Raspler

subject: series
synopsis: Shin'ichi Sakamoto's climbing manga: loner Buntaro Mori finds meaning only on sheer rock faces, building toward a solo winter ascent of K2's east face.

subject: series
synopsis: The Incredible Hulk annuals (1968-1994): Steranko's cover for #1, Englehart and Starlin specials, and crossover extras.
author: Doug Moench

subject: series
synopsis: Paul Malmont's 2010 Doc Savage for DC's First Wave line: the Man of Bronze and his crew in a pulp-noir world shared with the Spirit and Batman.

subject: series
synopsis: James Asmus's 2012 Gambit: Remy LeBeau returns to thievery in globetrotting heists.

subject: series
synopsis: The fourth volume of Love and Rockets (2016-), Gilbert and Jaime Hernandez's return to the comic-book format with Palomar and Locas stories.

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's 2012 American Judge Dredd by Duane Swierczynski and Nelson Daniel, a fresh take on Mega-City One's lawman.

subject: series
synopsis: Judd Winick's short 2009 Exiles relaunch: Blink leads displaced heroes repairing broken realities.

subject: series
synopsis: Geoff Johns and Gary Frank's post-apocalyptic series about a man transformed by nuclear radiation who becomes a glowing protector in a ruined Las Vegas, guarding a family in a world overrun by warlords and mutants.
author: Geoff Johns

subject: series
synopsis: Bob Haney and Ramona Fradon's campy 1960s Metamorpho: adventurer Rex Mason, turned into the Element Man, quarrels with Simon Stagg.

subject: series
synopsis: Paul Cornell's New 52 Stormwatch: Apollo, Midnighter and Martian Manhunter in a secret team guarding Earth from cosmic threats.

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Waid, Tom Peyer and Barry Kitson's 1999 mini tracing Barry Allen and Hal Jordan's friendship across their Silver Age team-ups.
author: Tom Peyer, Mark Waid

subject: series
synopsis: Bendis's Ultimate Comics Spider-Man (2009-2011) with David Lafuente and Sara Pichelli, culminating in the Death of Spider-Man.

subject: series
synopsis: Omnibus collections of the acclaimed BPRD series, the sprawling horror epic following the Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense.
author: Mike Mignola

subject: series
synopsis: A 2023 revival of the classic British war comics anthology tradition, bringing back the Commando and Battle Picture Weekly-style war stories for a new audience while maintaining period authenticity.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Masayuki Taguchi's manga adaptation of Koushun Takami's controversial novel drops a class of junior high students onto an island and forces them to kill each other. A brutal, politically charged satire of authoritarian control that predated and influenced The Hunger Games.
author: Koushun Takami, Masayuki Taguchi

subject: series
synopsis: A Black Lightning miniseries set in a troubled urban environment where Jefferson Pierce confronts crime at the street level in his home community, exploring the character's roots and responsibility to his neighborhood. Tony Isabella reclaimed the character he created.
author: Tony Isabella

subject: series
synopsis: Aftershock Comics' horror series by Joe Pruett and Francesco Francavilla-influenced art team, adapting the real-world urban legend of the Black-Eyed Kids — pale, dark-eyed children who appear at doors asking to be let in. A solid genre horror comic built on genuine dread rather than shock value.
author: Joe Pruett

subject: series
synopsis: Gerry Duggan's 2020 Krakoa-era Cable series following young Cable — the teenage Nathan Summers created when the original Cable's timeline was disrupted — navigating the mutant nation of Krakoa with all the swagger of his older self but none of the decades of experience. A fun, energetic series that used the younger Cable well.
author: Gerry Duggan

subject: series
synopsis: Paul Cornell's critically acclaimed series featuring Captain Britain, Black Knight, and Spitfire defending Britain from supernatural threats, praised for its wit, heart, and the iconic 'Vampire State' arc.
author: Paul Cornell

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's reprints of Bud Sagendorf's 1940s-50s Dell Popeye comic books, slapstick sea-yarns with Olive Oyl, Wimpy and the Sea Hag.

subject: series
synopsis: DC's eight-issue Countdown tie-in series following Adam Strange, Animal Man, and Starfire returning from space, alongside a backup featuring Forerunner. Padded out by Countdown's need for tie-in material rather than driven by organic story necessity.
author: Adam Beechen

subject: series
synopsis: DC's Countdown tie-in series featuring new versions of Dr. Fate and Eclipso, with Steve Gerber writing the Fate backup that was tragically left unfinished when Gerber died. The Fate story especially has genuine emotional weight.
author: Steve Gerber

subject: series
synopsis: CrossGen Comics' anthology series showcasing characters from across their shared publishing universe — Sojourn, Meridian, Way of the Rat, Crux — in short introductory stories. A smart way to sample the publisher's diverse line.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: DC's oversized treasury-format anthology presenting standalone adventures of Superman, Batman, and the Justice League. An important prestige format experiment of the Bronze Age.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's series continuing Elektra's tenure as Daredevil in the post-Zdarsky era, following her as she establishes her own identity in the role rather than serving as a replacement for Matt Murdock. Features the Devil's Hands supporting cast and extends the revitalized Daredevil mythology into new territory.
author: Erica Schultz

subject: series
synopsis: The publishing umbrella for the initial wave of Krakoa-era titles following House of X / Powers of X, including Marauders, X-Force, Excalibur, New Mutants, Fallen Angels, and Hickman's X-Men, collectively reinventing the X-Men line.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Jim Starlin's series systematically killing Kirby's Fourth World characters as part of the Final Crisis buildup — controversial for the treatment of these beloved creations and for continuity contradictions with the main event series.
author: Jim Starlin

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel UK's 1992 series following Death's Head II, a biomechanical bounty hunter who absorbed the original Death's Head's appearance. Combines British sci-fi sensibility with Marvel superhero excess; notable as an early Dan Abnett credit.
author: Dan Abnett

subject: series
synopsis: David Hine's street-level series set in Mutant Town following Bishop as a detective policing a mutant neighborhood in New York, one of the most effectively grounded X-books of the early 2000s with a crime-drama sensibility.
author: David Hine

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's Infinity Comics digital series featuring Doctor Strange during the Last Days of Magic storyline, formatted for the vertical reading experience on Marvel Unlimited.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Akira Toriyama's foundational adventure manga following the young Son Goku on a quest for the seven Dragon Balls. The first half is a comedic martial arts adventure of remarkable lightness and invention; the definitive influence on decades of shonen manga.
author: Akira Toriyama

subject: series
synopsis: Grant Morrison's cosmic crisis event depicting Darkseid's victory and the death of the DC multiverse, written with Morrison's trademark density and challenging structure. Divisive but ambitious.
author: Grant Morrison

subject: series
synopsis: Vertigo's 1999-2001 horror anthology, three unrelated short tales per issue by creators such as Azzarello, Bruce Jones, Lansdale and Quitely.

subject: series
synopsis: The second half of Daniel Abraham and Mel Rubi's adaptation of Martin's A Clash of Kings continues the faithful visual translation of Westeros's war-torn politics, balancing the novel's massive ensemble with careful pacing. A solid middle chapter in the ambitious comics adaptation of A Song of Ice and Fire.
author: Daniel Abraham

subject: series
synopsis: John Allison's Boom Studios series follows three very different university flatmates — Esther, Susan, and Daisy — through the joys and disasters of British college life. Warm, witty, and deeply human, it's widely regarded as one of the best slice-of-life comics of the 2010s, with Max Sarin's expressive art perfectly complementing Allison's sharp dialogue.
author: John Allison

subject: series
synopsis: AC Comics' anthology series reprinting golden-age superhero comics from the public domain, featuring a rotating cast of costumed heroes from comics' earliest era. Part of AC Comics' broader mission to preserve and republish pre-code golden-age material for collectors and historians of the medium.
author: Various (golden age reprints)

subject: series
synopsis: Greg Pak and Fred Van Lente's 2011 series following Hercules stripped of his divine powers and living as a street-level Brooklyn hero protecting his community. A charming and often funny series that gave Hercules genuine vulnerability while maintaining his mythological grandeur.
author: Greg Pak, Fred Van Lente

subject: series
synopsis: Eric Powell's Appalachian folk horror following Rondel, a cursed witch-hunter wandering the dark hills of a mythological American frontier, facing devils, curses, and the spirits of a brutally harsh land.
author: Eric Powell

subject: series
synopsis: Image Comics' monthly preview magazine of interviews and first looks, serializing shorts such as Kirkman's Negan origin.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's all-ages Hulk series in the Marvel Adventures imprint, starring Bruce Banner and his Hulk persona in accessible, self-contained adventures aimed at younger readers. Written by Paul Benjamin, it successfully translated the Hulk's Jekyll-and-Hyde concept into a format that works well for children without losing the character's core appeal.
author: Paul Benjamin

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's premium hardcover reprints collecting the classic Stan Lee and Jack Kirby Captain America stories from Tales of Suspense and the character's first solo series — defining the modern Steve Rogers mythology and establishing Cap's trademark combination of idealism and tactical brilliance.
author: Stan Lee

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's premium hardcover reprints of the Lee-Kirby and Lee-Trimpe Incredible Hulk stories, collecting the surprisingly complex early mythology of Bruce Banner's gamma-spawned alter ego. Essential for understanding how Marvel built the modern Hulk character from its awkward first issues.
author: Stan Lee

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's Bronze Age black-and-white magazine anthology that debuted Star-Lord (issue #4) and Rocket Raccoon (issue #7), alongside cosmic stories featuring Guardians-adjacent characters. An important historical document for fans of the modern MCU cosmic heroes.
author: Roy Thomas

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's reprint series collecting the original 1950s Marvelman British comics — the precursor to Alan Moore's revolutionary reimagining — featuring the classic adventures of Micky Moran/Marvelman and the Marvelman Family in their original, all-ages Golden Age form.
author: Mick Anglo

subject: series
synopsis: Katsuhiko Chiba's manga adaptation of the Gundam Wing storyline that incorporates Endless Waltz material, presenting an expanded version of the Wing saga's central conflict between the five Gundam pilots and the OZ organization.
author: Katsuhiko Chiba

subject: series
synopsis: Naoki Urasawa's psychological thriller following a German surgeon who saves the life of a boy who grows up to become a serial killer, and his obsessive hunt across Europe to stop him. A slow-burn masterwork of plotting, character, and moral philosophy — among the greatest manga ever made.
author: Naoki Urasawa

subject: series
synopsis: Marjorie Liu and Sana Takeda's lush dark fantasy following a young woman with a monstrous power in a matriarchal world at war — winner of multiple Eisner Awards and visually among the most gorgeous comics of the 2010s.
author: Marjorie Liu

subject: series
synopsis: Ryosuke Takeuchi and Hikaru Miyoshi's clever crime manga reimagines Moriarty as a 19th century aristocratic reformer using crime to dismantle Britain's class system, before his inevitable collision with Sherlock Holmes. A stylish and politically engaged take on the Doyle canon.
author: Ryosuke Takeuchi

subject: series
synopsis: Tie-in comics to the acclaimed animated series following a younger, more optimistic Clark Kent at the Daily Planet alongside Lois Lane and Jimmy Olsen. Captures the show's warm energy and refreshingly earnest take on Superman's early years, making it approachable for new readers and nostalgic for fans of the series.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: AC Comics' long-running series starring Nightveil, a Golden Age public-domain superheroine reimagined and revived, became one of the publisher's flagship characters. Primarily of interest to collectors of classic-era heroines and fans of AC's extensive Golden Age preservation work.

subject: series
synopsis: Dynamite's first Red Sonja ongoing (2005-2013): Michael Avon Oeming and Mel Rubi relaunch the she-devil with a sword in Hyrkanian adventures.

subject: series
synopsis: Al Ewing's four-issue post-Krakoa series resurrecting Erik Lehnsherr with careful attention to the ideological and personal weight of Magneto's history, delivered through horror-tinged storytelling that treats the character's tragedy with appropriate gravity.
author: Al Ewing

subject: series
synopsis: Al Ewing's Krakoa-era Marvel series following the Sentient Weapon Observation and Response Division, led by Magneto and Abigail Brand. A tightly plotted sci-fi thriller that builds on Ewing's Immortal Hulk approach — dense, surprising, and quietly devastating.
author: Al Ewing

subject: series
synopsis: Brian K. Vaughan and Fiona Staples' space opera epic following Marko and Alana — soldiers from warring alien races — who fall in love and have a child, then spend years on the run from both their governments across a galaxy teeming with bizarre life. Widely considered one of the greatest comics of its era.
author: Brian K. Vaughan

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's rotating team concept — Dr. Strange assembles a different lineup of heroes for each arc — produced an uneven but occasionally inspired anthology of superhero adventures. Notable for spotlighting overlooked characters like Thunderstrike and USAgent.
author: Tom Brevoort

subject: series
synopsis: Acclaim's 1997 Shadowman: Jamie Delano reinvents the voodoo hero with a new host, Mike LeRoi, in grim supernatural horror.

subject: series
synopsis: Peter David and Rick Leonardi's 1992 Spider-Man 2099: geneticist Miguel O'Hara battles the corporation Alchemax in a corporate-run Nueva York.
author: Peter David, Evan Skolnick

subject: series
synopsis: Udon Entertainment's Street Fighter comics adapting and expanding the video game universe — the gold standard of licensed Street Fighter comics, with detailed action art and faithful character portrayal.
author: Ken Siu-Chong

subject: series
synopsis: Archival reprints of the classic Jerry Siegel and Joe Shuster Superman newspaper strips.
author: Jerry Siegel

subject: series
synopsis: Issei Eifuku and Taiyo Matsumoto's Edo-period tale of a gentle, enigmatic samurai who carries only a bamboo sword, drawn in Matsumoto's singular style.

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's reprint collections of the Archie Comics TMNT Adventures series (1988–1995), the licensed tie-in to the original animated series that eventually developed its own distinct storylines, environmental themes, and original characters. Beloved by fans of the cartoon era for striking a balance between kids' entertainment and genuine storytelling ambition.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Raoul Cauvin and Willy Lambil's long-running Belgian comics series set during the American Civil War, following the misadventures of bumbling Union soldiers Blutch and Chesterfield. Mixes black comedy with genuine human drama about the absurdity of war.
author: Raoul Cauvin

subject: series
synopsis: James Tynion IV and Martin Simmonds' acclaimed horror thriller about a government agency that controls what conspiracy theories gain enough belief to become real, following a new recruit grappling with the terrifying implications. Modern paranoia horror at its finest.
author: James Tynion IV

subject: series
synopsis: The controversial series crowning Bart Allen as the new Flash, criticized for aging up the character and the grim handling of his tenure and death. A misstep that quickly reversed course and returned Barry Allen to the role.
author: Danny Bilson

synopsis: DC/Hanna-Barbera's crossover title pairing the Stone Age Flintstones with the futuristic Jetsons in lighthearted adventures that worked around the inherent comedic absurdity of the premise. A piece of licensed comics nostalgia aimed primarily at fans of both classic animated series.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Valiant's Ank series following an immortal man who has walked through history and now navigates time threats in the Valiant Universe.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Mike Carey and Alex Ross's limited series about Jim Hammond, the original Human Torch — an android who predates all other Marvel heroes — reactivated in the modern day and grappling with what it means to be human. Ross's involvement ensures a prestige visual standard.
author: Mike Carey

subject: series
synopsis: Hardcover reprints of the all-new X-Men from Giant-Size X-Men #1: Claremont with Cockrum, Byrne and Paul Smith — Phoenix, Dark Phoenix, Days of Future Past.
author: Chris Claremont, Barry Windsor-Smith

subject: series
synopsis: Rumiko Takahashi's iconic early sci-fi romantic comedy introduces Lum, an alien princess who falls for the lecherous Ataru Moroboshi after he grabs her horns in a global tag game, claiming her as his bride. The series that launched Takahashi's career and established many rom-com manga conventions.
author: Rumiko Takahashi

subject: series
synopsis: DC's comprehensive loose-leaf encyclopedia published in 1990 updating the original Who's Who series, providing profiles, character histories, and visual references for the full DC Universe cast. An invaluable reference for the post-Crisis DC continuity, still consulted by fans and researchers of that era.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Harvey Comics' licensed series featuring Walter Lantz's iconic animated woodpecker character, continuing the slapstick comedy adventures of the red-crested troublemaker and his cast of recurring antagonists.

synopsis: Richard D. Nolane and Maza's alternate history in which WWII drags on into 1946, fought by Luftwaffe pilots in revolutionary jets and flying wings.
author: Nolane

subject: series
synopsis: Inio Asano's action thriller about a young ninja in a near-future Tokyo where ninja clans still operate in the shadows.
